age.evidence: Both sexes of mice aged 1-2 months were used.

sex.evidence: Both sexes of mice aged 1-2 months were used.

dosing.evidence: TBG or fluoxetine hydrochloride ... was administered to the mouse intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a dosage of 10 mg/kg of bodyweight. USP-grade saline (0.9%) was used as vehicle.

handling.evidence: it was also handled 10 min daily for 3 days ... The mouse was handled 5-10 min per day for 3 days to habituate it to the experimenter.

group_housing.evidence: Mice were group-housed with littermates and maintained on a 12 h light/dark cycle.

day_night_flipped.evidence: maintained on a 12 h light/dark cycle (direction not specified)

assays.assay_description: Custom plexiglass EPM (arms 30 x 5 cm; closed arms walled 15 cm; elevated 50 cm). Mice freely explored for 5 min. DeepLabCut tracked multiple body points; total distance and time in open vs. closed arms quantified.

application_type.evidence: TBG ... was administered to the mouse intraperitoneally (i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Habituation to the EPM apparatus before testing is not described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Each mouse was allowed to explore the EPM freely for 5 min.

food_restriction.evidence: No food was placed in the EPM during the 5-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: No water was placed in the EPM during the 5-min test.

time_to_assay.evidence: injected a single dose of TBG (10 mg/kg) into the mice immediately after 7d UMS and conducted behavioral tests one day later

sample_size.evidence: n = number of mice unless otherwise indicated

outcomes.summary: UMS mice spent less time in open arms than controls, with similar total distance. A single 10 mg/kg i.p. dose of TBG administered after UMS restored open-arm time, indicating reduced anxiety.
outcomes.statistics: Time in open arms: H(3) = 8.275, p < 0.05, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc. Total distance: H(3) = 4.437, p = 0.1088.

B1_num_measures.evidence: quantify the total distance traveled and the time spent in open vs. closed arms

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Data reported as totals over the 5-min session.

B4_ethological.evidence: Measures locomotor distance and zone occupancy time.

B6_cognitive.evidence: EPM assesses innate anxiety, not learning.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: DeepLabCut was used only to track body points; behaviour was quantified from body location (zone time, distance), not classified into behavioural states.

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are not considered enclosed refuges by rubric definition.

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms are open-ended extensions of a central platform (rubric).

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the apparatus during the 5-min test.

D3_recording_days.evidence: tested one day after UMS termination

D5_followup.evidence: Behavioural tests one day (24 h) after TBG injection.

assays.assay_description: Free-moving mice in a 38x28x23 cm chamber explore two textured columns. Protocol: habituation (3 min), encoding (5 min, two identical textures), resting (5 min), testing (3 min, familiar + novel texture). Approaches, investigation time and discrimination index (DI) scored with Boris.

setup_habituation.evidence: Prior to testing, the subject mouse was habituated to the testing chamber ... for 10 min per day for 2 days.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in apparatus during test.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in apparatus during test.

time_to_assay.evidence: conducted behavioral tests one day later

sample_size.evidence: n = number of mice unless otherwise indicated

outcomes.summary: Control mice preferred the novel texture (positive DI); UMS abolished this preference; TBG restored novel-texture preference. Total exploration during encoding was similar across groups.
outcomes.statistics: DI testing: H(3) = 16.061, p < 0.001, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc.
outcomes.evidence: while control mice preferred the novel texture, UMS mice lost such preference ... TBG ... restored the novel texture preference in WTD

B1_num_measures.evidence: quantified the number of approaches and the amount of time spent actively investigating the columns, and computed the discrimination index

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Totals/indices over phase; no within-session time course.

B4_ethological.evidence: Approaches and active investigation (sniffing/whisking) of textured columns scored as discrete exploratory acts using Boris.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Requires memory of the encoded texture to distinguish familiar vs. novel during testing.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Behaviour analyzed offline with Boris (manual annotation tool).

D1_continuity.evidence: All phases on one testing day.

D2_session_duration.evidence: habituation (3 min), encoding (5 min), resting (5 min), and testing (3 min) — 16 min total within single test session.

assays.assay_description: Food-restricted mice in a four-quadrant arena (12'x12'x9' acrylic, internal walls) learn to dig in scented pine-shaving ramekins for a Cheerio reward (discrimination phase: rosemary/clove/thyme/nutmeg), then thyme is swapped for cinnamon (reversal). Criterion = 8/10 correct trials. Outcome: trials to criterion per phase.

setup_restrain.evidence: mouse could freely explore the arena

food_restriction.evidence: The mouse was food restricted starting ~5 days before the testing day so that its body weight was reduced to 80-85% of the baseline.

time_to_assay.evidence: conducted behavioral tests one day later

sample_size.evidence: n = number of mice unless otherwise indicated

outcomes.summary: UMS did not alter initial discrimination but significantly increased trials to criterion in the reversal phase. A single dose of TBG normalized reversal performance, restoring cognitive flexibility.
outcomes.statistics: Initial discrimination: F(2,13)=0.8922, p=0.4334. Reversal: H(3)=9.954, p<0.01, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc.
outcomes.evidence: UMS mice ... took significantly more trials to learn the new odor-reward contingency in the reversal phase ... TBG ... normalized cognitive flexibility in the 4-choice task

B1_num_measures.evidence: Number of trials taken to reach the performance criterion in the initial discrimination and reversal phase.

B4_ethological.evidence: Digging in scented media for buried food is a natural species-typical foraging behaviour scored as the operational response.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Evaluates the mouse's flexibility in learning an odor-reward contingency and reversing the association.

E3_bedding.evidence: Digging media were made of pine shavings ... in ramekins inside the arena.

E6_spatial.evidence: 4 quadrants partially divided by 3'-wide internal walls

E8_food_water.evidence: Food rewards were small pieces (~10 mg each) of Honey Nut Cheerio delivered in the apparatus.

D1_continuity.evidence: discrimination session followed by a reversal session on the testing day

D2_session_duration.evidence: Trials untimed; most mice completed shaping within 1 h, and testing similarly extends beyond 15 min in this paradigm.

D4_baseline.evidence: Pre-training is not a recorded baseline for this assay.

assays.assay_description: Head-fixed mice in a Neurotar mobile home cage explore textures (sandpaper patches) attached to the cage wall. Phases: free exploration (5 min), encoding (15 min, two identical textures), resting (10 min), testing (15 min, familiar + novel). Approaches, interaction time, and DI scored with Boris. Performed concurrently with 2-photon calcium imaging of S1BF L2/3 neurons.

setup_habituation.evidence: The mouse was handled 5-10 min per day for 3 days ... habituated to head-fixation on the empty MHC (1 h session x 2 per day for at least 6 days).

food_restriction.evidence: No food in MHC during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in MHC during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: conducted behavioral tests one day later

sample_size.evidence: n = number of mice unless otherwise indicated

outcomes.summary: Total interaction time was similar across groups, but UMS impaired discrimination index and TBG restored novel-texture preference. Calcium imaging showed novel-texture-selective neuronal responses were reduced by UMS and rescued by TBG.
outcomes.statistics: DI: F(2,32)=10.95, p<0.001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc. Total interaction time: F(2,32)=1.487, p=0.2412.
outcomes.evidence: UMS impaired texture discrimination and TBG rescued it ... neither UMS nor post-stress TBG treatment altered total interaction time

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total interaction time and discrimination index reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Active whisker-investigation of textures scored as discrete exploratory acts.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Requires memory of the encoded texture to identify novelty.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: analyzed offline using the Boris program (manual annotation).

E1_environment_type.evidence: Neurotar mobile home cage used as a head-fixed test apparatus.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water in MHC during recording.

D1_continuity.evidence: All four phases completed in one session.

D2_session_duration.evidence: free exploration (5 min) + encoding (15 min) + resting (10 min) + testing (15 min) = 45 min

judge_notes: Kept four behavioural assays: EPM, free-moving WTD, four-choice odor discrimination/reversal, and head-fixed WTD. The head-fixed WTD is genuinely a distinct paradigm from the free-moving WTD (different apparatus, head-fixation, different protocol durations) so was kept separate per gptoss/glm.
Excluded all neural-only readouts (wide-field Ca imaging of CaWF, 2P Ca imaging of baseline synchronous events, in vitro patch-clamp of PV+ INs) and spine imaging — these are not behavioural assays.

Overrode glm's B7=Yes for EPM: DeepLabCut was used purely as a position tracker (body point used to compute zone time and distance), not as a behavioural classifier — rubric requires classification of discrete states, so scored 0.

B4 for WTD assays scored Yes: active whisker-mediated investigation/sniffing of textures, scored as discrete approach/investigation events with Boris, falls within the ethological-behaviour category. Digging in 4-choice also scored ethological.
B6 for WTD scored Yes (requires memory of the encoded texture across the rest interval — a learned/memory component), aligning with how the literature treats novel-object/texture recognition.
D2 for free-moving WTD: total in-apparatus session (3+5+5+3 = 16 min) treated as a single session >=15 min, scored 1.
D2 for 4-choice scored 1 with low confidence — paper states sessions were untimed but most mice completed shaping within 1 h, supporting >=15 min for the full discrimination+reversal session.
DOI taken from candidate consensus (qwen, glm); gptoss left it null but the value is consistent with the paper's supplementary link.
